newsitem.title: CANADA: Amoco starts Canada east coast offshore well.
newsitem.headline: Amoco starts Canada east coast offshore well.

text.p: Amoco Corp unit Amoco Canada Petroleum Co Ltd said on Friday it started drilling its West Bonne Bay oil prospect off the east coast of Canada.

The well, expected to reach a total depth of 4,350 metres (14,270 ft) in three to four months, is about 15 km (9 miles) northeast of the Terra Nova oil field and 40 km (25 miles) southeast of the Hibernia field in the Jeane d'Arc basin.
Amoco is operator and has an 80 percent interest in the exploration play. Partners include Petro-Canada and Norsk Hydro with 10 percent each.
The well, whose costs were estimated at C$40 million, is being drilled by Sedco Forex's Bill Shoemaker semi-submersible rig, which was modified to operate on the Grand Banks of Newfoundland.
Oil reserves at West Bonne Bay have been estimated at as high as 300 million barrels. ((Jeffrey Jones, Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
